sections.content: [Placeholder passage text about Henry Moore: After leaving school Moore became a teacher (as his father wished), then studied at Leeds School of Art (not sculpture in first term). The Royal College of Art's sculpture teaching was poor when he arrived. Moore read about ancient sculpture from books in the library, then visited the British Museum. The Trocadero Museum's Mayan Chac Mool sculpture had an impact on Moore — he felt it was different from European stone sculpture. He joined Unit One (artists who wanted to promote modern art). 1930s: exhibition at Leicester Galleries criticised; Moore urged to resign/offer his resignation. 1940s: materials unavailable so drew instead; drew miners in Castleford (hometown); commissioned for a Madonna and Child sculpture; American collectors started buying; increased wealth enabled more ambitious work. 1950s: bronze reclining figures marked new style.]

sections.content: [Placeholder passage text about fairy tales and Tehrani: Tehrani used phylogenetic analysis (methods from evolutionary biology) to study 58 fairy tale variants of Little Red Riding Hood. He tested whether links/relationships existed among the stories, found that certain story elements (events/characters) changed over time, that the middle of the story was no more important than other parts, and that moral lessons/warnings were not the key to survival. The most important aspect for survival was plot (specifically horror/scary content). Jack Zipes suggests that story features only survive if they have deeper significance. Tehrani referred to Chinese and Japanese fairy tales (featuring crime) to add more evidence for Zipes' ideas. Mathias Clasen believes fairy tales provide a safe way to deal with fear. The story stems: details of the plot may change; Tehrani rejects the idea that useful lessons are the reason for survival; various theories about social significance of fairy tales lack factual basis; insights into development of fairy tales may come through biological methods; all the stories analysed were originally spoken not written.]
